\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تفتیش} (taftīsh)}{تفتیش (taftīsh)}]{\ur{تفتیش} (taftīsh) — an investigation}

\label{lesson:UR-C282-taftish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crook, then the Urdu for forged.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تفتیش}}
\textbf{\ur{تفتیش}} — \emph{taftīsh} — \textquotedblleft{}an investigation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{تفتیش} \ur{میں} \ur{ایک} \ur{مہینہ} \ur{لگا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taftīsh meṅ ek mahīnā lagā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The investigation took a month.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تفتیش}} (\emph{taftīsh}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taftīsh}, \textquotedblleft{}a searching, an inspection\textquotedblright{}. It is the word of police reports and the news.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taftīsh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taftīsh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taftīsh meṅ ek mahīnā lagā.} — The investigation took a month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a crook, then the Urdu for forged, then say \emph{taftīsh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{تفتیش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An investigation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سراغ} (surāgh)}{سراغ (surāgh)}]{\ur{سراغ} (surāgh) — a clue; a trace}

\label{lesson:UR-C282-suragh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for forged, then the Urdu for an investigation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سراغ}}
\textbf{\ur{سراغ}} — \emph{surāgh} — \textquotedblleft{}a clue; a trace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{سراغ} \ur{ملا} \ur{تو} \ur{پولیس} \ur{آئے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar surāgh milā to polīs āe gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If a clue turns up, the police will come.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سراغ}} (\emph{surāgh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{surāgh}, \textquotedblleft{}a trace, a track\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{سراغ} \ur{ملا}} says a clue was found; \textbf{\ur{سراغ} \ur{لگانا}} is to track something down.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جاسوس} (jāsūs)}{جاسوس (jāsūs)}]{\ur{جاسوس} (jāsūs) — a detective; a spy}

\label{lesson:UR-C282-jasus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an investigation, then the Urdu for a clue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جاسوس}}
\textbf{\ur{جاسوس}} — \emph{jāsūs} — \textquotedblleft{}a detective; a spy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جاسوس} \ur{نے} \ur{سب} \ur{کچھ} \ur{دیکھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jāsūs ne sab kuchh dekhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The detective saw everything.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جاسوس}} (\emph{jāsūs}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{jāsūs}, \textquotedblleft{}a spy\textquotedblright{}. In stories it is the detective who works out who did it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ثبوت} (subūt)}{ثبوت (subūt)}]{\ur{ثبوت} (subūt) — proof; evidence}

\label{lesson:UR-C282-subut}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a clue, then the Urdu for a detective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ثبوت}}
\textbf{\ur{ثبوت}} — \emph{subūt} — \textquotedblleft{}proof; evidence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پولیس} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{کوئی} \ur{ثبوت} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīs ke pās koī subūt nahīṅ thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police had no proof.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ثبوت}} (\emph{subūt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{thubūt}, \textquotedblleft{}firmness, a being established\textquotedblright{}: what makes a claim stand. Urdu says its first letter as \emph{s}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈھونڈنا} (ḍhūnḍnā)}{ڈھونڈنا (ḍhūnḍnā)}]{\ur{ڈھونڈنا} (ḍhūnḍnā) — to look for}

\label{lesson:UR-C282-dhundna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a detective, then the Urdu for proof.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈھونڈنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈھونڈنا}} — \emph{ḍhūnḍnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to look for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پولیس} \ur{نے} \ur{ہر} \ur{جگہ} \ur{چور} \ur{کو} \ur{ڈھونڈا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīs ne har jagah chor ko ḍhūnḍā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police looked for the thief everywhere.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{چابی} \ur{ڈھونڈی}, \emph{us ne chābī ḍhūnḍī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ḍhū̃ḍhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6839). Urdu writes the second \emph{ḍ} without the breath: \textbf{\ur{ڈھونڈنا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍhūnḍnā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a detective, then the Urdu for proof, then say \emph{ḍhūnḍnā} again
\end{itemize}
